title: Memory maintenance: dry-run plan, checkpointed auto steps and approval for the rest (#1390)
body:
Fixes #1390.

I added `node-bot/memory-maintenance.js`, one coordinated retention pass over the memory stores. Authoritative data (sessions, facts) is never deleted: sessions are moved to `archive/sessions`, old fact-log lines to `archive/facts-log-<year>.jsonl`, and only derived indexes or approved graph history are dropped.

**Runs on its own (auto)**
- `reconcile-search`: removes search rows (keyword and vector) of sessions whose file no longer exists. New `listSessionIds()` / `removeSessions()` in session-search-index.js, one transaction.
- `reconcile-entities`: drops entity-index mentions of deleted sessions (and entities left empty). Backed up first.
- `archive-facts-log`: moves fact-log lines older than 180 days into the archive. `getFactHistory` now reads the archive files too, so history stays complete. Backed up first; unparseable lines stay in the live log and are reported.

**Needs my approval (step id in `approve`)**
- `archive-session`: moves sessions not updated in 365 days to `archive/sessions`. Kept (with the reason reported): sessions needed by an active, pending or pinned fact or a standing intent (via `sessionId` / `origin.sessionId`), parents of retained forks, corrupt files, and everything if facts.json can't be read.
- `prune-graph-history`: deletes closed edge windows older than 365 days. `memory-graph.db` is backed up first with `db.backup`.

**Measure only:** snapshots, self-work traces and the tool-call log are reported in `stores` with their existing bound, nothing is done to them.

**Plan and run**
- `plan()` is a dry run: store sizes, steps with kind/target/reason/bytes, and what is kept and why.
- `run({ mode, approve, signal })` writes `maintenance/checkpoint.json` before and after each step, in order, with the step's backup in `maintenance/backup/<planId>/`. A step that throws is restored from its backup, marked failed, and the rest are skipped. A cancelled pass (signal) leaves the checkpoint and the next run resumes it; a step caught mid-way (process died) is restored and redone. Only the latest plan's backups are kept. Refuses to run while gaming.

**Wiring**
- server.js: after the pending-fact expiry in the idle consolidation, auto steps run at most once per 24 h, inside `resourceCoordinator.run({ owner: "Memory maintenance", background: true })` when it exists. Not built in tests.
- `GET /admin/memory/maintenance` (the plan) and `POST /admin/memory/maintenance/run` `{ approve: [ids] }`, admin-protected, in memory-facts-capability.js.
- Doctor: a "Memory maintenance" line (last run, failed step, proposals waiting).

**Limits**
- The graph prune is one SQL transaction, so a failure leaves the db unchanged; its backup is for me to restore by hand, not restored automatically. Archived sessions are not re-indexed if moved back by hand.
- The approval is the step id, and the targets are re-derived when it runs (same rules), not a frozen list.
- Measure-only stores are read from their default locations beside acp-memory; env overrides aren't followed.
- A session file is parsed once per plan; fine for hundreds, would want an index for thousands.
- The in-memory approval-gate queue is not consulted; sessions behind pending facts are kept, which is what pending approvals pin.

Tests: `node-bot/test/memory-maintenance.test.js` (temp dirs only) covers active/pinned/intent/pending references, corrupt log lines and session files, cancel then resume, a throwing step restored from backup, interrupted-step recovery, auto vs approved, fact history staying complete after archiving, search reconcile touching only deleted sessions, and graph prune needing approval and backing up first. I did not run the suite locally; CI does.
interface: The merged change for PR #1400 is covered by test/memory-maintenance.test.js.
why: Additional real merged-fix benchmark case selected to broaden the agentic coding evaluation.
